set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: State 5 coverage of store_spool
set_aside.text: One public operation per State 3 capability ... Candidate public capabilities: spool_entry_name, spool_attempt_prefix, publish_spool_entry, read_spool_entry, discard_spool_attempt, remove_spool_group, remove_spool_temporaries
set_aside.question: What are the State 5 inputs, outputs, errors, effects and exact callers of each new store_spool capability?
options: Add one State 5 public-operation contract for each capability
Declare some names private implementation helpers and contract only the capabilities store calls
set_aside.default_guess: Treat all seven listed capabilities as public to store and add explicit contracts for them.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool initialization and spool root
set_aside.text: The spool's on-disk layout below the spool area and the run directory ... Candidate public capabilities: spool_entry_name ... remove_spool_temporaries
set_aside.question: How does store_spool receive or retain the spool-area root and any open directory handles, given that no constructor, open operation or root argument is specified?
options: store constructs a store_spool object with an opened spool-root handle
Every store_spool operation receives an opened root handle
store_spool derives the root from a path supplied to each call
set_aside.default_guess: Have store construct the companion once with an opened spool-root directory handle.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: spool_entry_name and spool_attempt_prefix
set_aside.text: the name of a spooled file inside its run's spool directory, made from its SpooledFileKey ... an emitted, injective file layout with exact attempt prefixes and bounded names
set_aside.question: What exact input key types and output forms do spool_entry_name and spool_attempt_prefix use, and what relationship must hold between an attempt prefix and every entry name belonging to that attempt?
options: Return opaque relative-name values from the full SpooledFile key and attempt key
Return path components as strings with a specified encoding
Remove these operations from the public boundary and keep naming wholly internal
set_aside.default_guess: Use opaque validated relative-name types, with every entry name for an attempt beginning with the exact prefix returned for that attempt.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry
set_aside.text: publishing one file complete, fsynced and digest-checked by a temporary and a rename, replacing a file at the same position; the two spool ceilings of A20, checked on publishing
set_aside.question: What does publish_spool_entry receive and return, where are the expected digest and size computed, what failures distinguish a ceiling refusal from symlink or I/O failure, and at what point is the file considered published?
options: Receive key, bytes, expected digest and size; return file facts or ceiling refusal/internal error
Receive key and bytes; compute and return digest and size itself
Receive a staged file plus expected facts and publish it
set_aside.default_guess: Pass the key, bytes and caller-computed expected digest and size; return verified file facts, a distinct ceiling refusal, or an internal failure.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: spool ceiling accounting during replacement
set_aside.text: the run's spooled files plus this one against spool_run_bytes_max ... replacing a file at the same position
set_aside.question: When publishing replaces an unnamed file already at the same position, is that old file's size subtracted before applying spool_run_bytes_max, and exactly which completed, temporary, recorded and unrecorded files count toward the run total?
options: Count all completed spool entries, subtracting the replaced entry; exclude temporaries
Count every file below the run spool, including temporaries
Count only files named by SpooledFile records
set_aside.default_guess: Count all completed spool entries whether recorded or unnamed, exclude temporaries, and subtract the entry being replaced.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool.read_spool_entry
set_aside.text: reading a file back checked against a digest and size
set_aside.question: What identity and expected facts does read_spool_entry receive, what bytes or metadata does it return, and how does it distinguish a missing entry, a symlink, an unreadable file and a digest or size mismatch so store.read_value_bytes can produce its fixed errors?
options: Receive the spool key plus expected digest and size and return bytes or a typed storage failure
Receive a SpooledFile record and return bytes
Receive only the key and recover expected facts from sidecar metadata
set_aside.default_guess: Receive the key, expected digest and expected size from store and return bytes or a typed internal-storage failure.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool.discard_spool_attempt
set_aside.text: discarding every file of the refused attempt ... Candidate public capabilities ... discard_spool_attempt
set_aside.question: Does publish_spool_entry itself atomically discard the attempt on a ceiling refusal, or must store call discard_spool_attempt after receiving the refusal; and what happens if that discard is interrupted or fails?
options: publish_spool_entry performs the complete discard before returning the ceiling refusal
store must call discard_spool_attempt after a ceiling refusal
discard_spool_attempt is private and used internally by publish_spool_entry
set_aside.default_guess: Make discard_spool_attempt private to store_spool and require publish_spool_entry to complete the attempt discard before returning a ceiling refusal.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_group
set_aside.text: removing one run's spool ... Candidate public capabilities ... remove_spool_group
set_aside.question: What identifies the group, is removal idempotent when it is absent, and what result or error does it return so store.remove_run_spool can preserve its specified idempotence and ignored-removal-failure behavior?
options: Take run_id and return done or an I/O failure, with absence treated as done
Take an opaque spool-group key and return a best-effort result
Never report removal failures
set_aside.default_guess: Take run_id, treat absence as success, and return an I/O failure that store maps to internal_error while runs ignores it as specified.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: store_spool.remove_spool_temporaries and open_store
set_aside.text: start-time removal of temporary files ... removing the temporaries an interrupted publish left ... A failed check creates and removes nothing
set_aside.question: Does store.open_store call remove_spool_temporaries, which temporary names and scope may it remove, and must the symlink/private-directory checks complete before any removal so a failed start check changes nothing?
options: open_store delegates a whole-spool cleanup after all start checks pass
store_spool cleanup is part of its own initialization before open_store returns
Only temporaries discovered within each run group are removed lazily
set_aside.default_guess: Have open_store first complete all start checks, then call store_spool to remove only names recognized as spool publish temporaries across the spool area.
